St. 1, Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date August 11, 1941

SUBJECT: Application of D.S.I. Ma Hsin Chen
for transfer from Special Branch to
Crime Branch.

With reference to the attached application
of D.S.I. Ma Hsin Chen for transfer from the
Special Branch to the Crime Branch, he states
that in view of the fact that he is unable to
write reports in English he cannot assist D.I. Rae
and D.S.I. Loh in executive work as he would like
to do and therefore he considers his particular
abilities would be given more scope in station
work.

Following the recent transfer to the
Uniform Branch of three experienced clerks who
had been assisting in executive work, this office
has been experiencing considerable difficulties
and is in urgent need of an efficient executive
officer.

It is therefore respectfully suggested
that an intelligent and capable English speaking
Chinese Sub-Inspector be transferred to the
staff of S. 1 to understudy D.I. Rae and D.S.I.
Loh, in place of D.S.I. Ma Hsin Chen.

A very suitable man would be either
Sub-Inspector Li Shu Fa, at present attached to
Gordon Road Station, or Sub-Inspector Wu Sih
Chuan attached to Pestee Road Station.

（批：S.B. (crs B). I agree.）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH AUG 11 1941）

W. E. Wilson
D. S. I.

A.C. (Special Branch)

关于随附的副探长马新臣 (Ma Hsin Chen) 从特别处调往刑事处的申请，他在申请中表示，鉴于他无法用英文撰写报告，他不能像他希望的那样协助探长雷 (Rae) 和副探长罗 (Loh) 处理行政工作，因此他认为他的特殊才能在捕房工作中能得到更充分的发挥。

由于近期三名曾协助处理行政工作的经验丰富的文员被调往制服部门，本办公室一直面临相当大的困难，急需一名高效的行政官员。

因此，谨建议调派一名聪明能干、会说英语的华人副督察至第1站工作人员中，作为探长雷 (Rae) 和副探长罗 (Loh) 的见习助手，以取代副探长马新臣 (Ma Hsin Chen)。

非常合适的人选可以是目前隶属于戈登路捕房的副督察李树法 (Li Shu Fa)，或者是隶属于贝勒路 (Pestee Road) 捕房的副督察吴思川 (Wu Sih Chuan)。

（批：特别处 (crs B)。我同意。）

Sir,
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY June 18, 1941. 875- 20 6 41）

With reference to the attached suggestion
of the D.C. (Chinese), I have discussed with senior
Chinese members of the Special Branch the alternative
proposition of replacing the recently appointed clerks
of the Special Branch with more experienced clerks
from stations. These senior members assure me that
no benefit would be derived from the suggested change
because, apart from their preference for station work,
station clerks are not familiar with the work of the
Special Branch and it would take considerable time to
train them.

What is really required at the present time
to cope with the difficulties now being encountered
is an experienced man with knowledge of Police work
to assist D. I. Kao and D.S.I. Loh in dealing with
labour problems during the time that the newly appointed
clerks are undergoing training.

The situation at present is that in the event
of the absence from duty of D.I. Kao or D.S.I. Loh
due to sickness, leave or any other reason, the working
of the Special Branch, Section 1, would be seriously
impaired as there is at present no-one on the staff
of the Section, since the transfer of those three
experienced clerks from S. 1 to the executive branch
on June 1, 1941, sufficiently experienced to undertake
the duties of D.I. Kao or D.S.I. Loh.

In view of the present acute shortage of
supervising staff at stations, the following suggestion
is put forward for favour of consideration as an
page_data.zh:
副总监（刑事及特别处）。
先生，
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处登记室 1941年6月18日。 875- 1941年6月20日）

关于随附的华务副总监的建议，我已与特别处的资深华籍成员讨论了另一种方案，即用来自各捕房的更有经验的文员替换特别处最近任命的那些文员。这些资深成员向我保证，建议的变更不会带来任何好处，因为除了他们更喜欢捕房工作外，捕房文员不熟悉特别处的工作，培训他们需要相当长的时间。

目前真正需要以应对当前遇到的困难的，是一名拥有警务工作知识的经验丰富的人员，在新任命的文员接受培训期间，协助高探长 (D. I. Kao) 和罗副探长 (D.S.I. Loh) 处理劳工问题。

目前的情况是，如果高探长或罗副探长因病、休假或其他原因缺勤，特别处第1股的运作将受到严重影响，因为自1941年6月1日那三名经验丰富的文员从第1站调往行政部门后，该股目前没有任何工作人员具备足够的经验来承担高探长或罗副探长的职责。

鉴于目前各捕房监督人员严重短缺，现提出以下建议供考虑，作为

page_data.en:
(2)

alternative solution of the problem:-
One Chinese Sub-Inspector could be employed
to supervise Rice Shops in Gordon Road and Pootoo
Road Districts instead of one Chinese Sub-Inspector
for each District as at present. As there are
50 S.M.C. Rice Dealers in Gordon Road District and
29 in Pootoo Road District, making a total of 79 in
the two districts, as against 74 in Sinsa District
and 77 in West Hongkew District, this would not
entail too much work for one man, and the Sub-Inspector
thus released could be employed temporarily to a
much greater advantage by this office.

R. H. Jabrum
P. A. to A.C.(Special Branch)

D. C. (Crime & Special Branches).
As far as the ranks of Sub-Inspector, Inspector & Chief Inspector are concerned the Special Branch is up to Establishment. Any additional personnel required to cope with increased work will naturally have to be found mostly from the Uniform Branch but due to the Foreign Branch resignations and retirements the Uniform Branch has felt the shortage in almost all sections of the Force of supervising staff acutely for some time. I have consulted D.O. "B" re suggestions in attached and he says he cannot deplete his Chinese Sub-Inspectors any further without disturbing routine efficiency. With about 50 men under training there is indeed a dearth of Sub-Inspectors. Only yesterday I could not arrange for one to be spared for certain special duties for the Traffic Branch.
As the immediate difficulties now encountered by the Special Branch seem to me to lie in the appointment of the clerks to Probationary Sub-Inspectors, I wonder if I could help by transferring or if Mr. Tabrum has in view any likely clerks with a few years experience in Police work in stations in exchange for the 'Griffins' recently appointed.

副总监（刑事及特别处）。
就副督察、督察及总督察的职级而言，特别处的人员编制已满。应对增加的工作量所需的任何额外人员，自然主要必须从制服部门抽调，但由于外侨科的辞职和退休，制服部门已在几乎所有警队部门中深切感受到监督人员短缺的问题有一段时间了。我就附件中的建议咨询了“B”分区督察，他说他不能再进一步抽调他的华人副督察，否则会扰乱日常效率。由于约有50人正在受训，确实缺乏副督察。就在昨天，我无法安排抽出一名人员去执行交通科的某些特殊任务。

S.I., Special Branch File No. Date June 7, 1941.

SUBJECT: Transfer of Chinese Sub-Inspector to Staff of Special Branch, S. 1

Following the recent transfer to the Uniform Branch of three experienced clerks who had been assisting in executive work, this office has been experiencing considerable difficulties and is in urgent need of the assistance of an efficient executive officer. It is therefore respectfully suggested that an intelligent and capable Chinese Sub-Inspector be transferred to the Staff of S. 1 to understudy D. I. Kao and D.S.I. Loh for a period of about six months. The three clerks newly transferred to this section are new employees, slow and without any office or Police experience.

The transfer of such a Sub-Inspector would enable the work to proceed smoothly whilst the new clerks are being trained.

A very suitable man would be Sub-Inspector Wu Sih Chuan, at present attached to Footoo Road Station. This man is approved by both C.D.I. Kuh and D.I. Kao, and his capabilities, which are of a high order, are known to the undersigned.

W. E. Wilcox
D. S. I.

A.C. (Special Branch)

副督察，特别处 档案号。 日期 1941年6月7日。

主题：调派华人副督察至特别处第1站工作人员

由于近期三名曾协助处理行政工作的经验丰富的文员被调往制服部门，本办公室一直面临相当大的困难，急需一名高效行政官员的协助。因此，谨建议调派一名聪明能干的华人副督察至第1站工作人员中，作为高探长 (D. I. Kao) 和罗副探长 (D.S.I. Loh) 的见习助手，为期约六个月。新调至该股的两名文员是新雇员，反应迟钝，且没有任何办公室或警务经验。

调派这样一名副督察将使工作在新文员接受培训期间顺利进行。

非常合适的人选是目前隶属于福煦路 (Footoo Road) 捕房的副督察吴思川 (Wu Sih Chuan)。此人得到了库总督察 (C.D.I. Kuh) 和高探长 (D.I. Kao) 的认可，且其出众的能力为签署人所知。

W. E. Wilcox

Date September 15, 1939

Subject. Recommendation for increase in pay for C.A. Zung Zoong Oen
attached to Section 1, Special Branch.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie

In view of his continuous good work and devotion
to duties which are both responsible and arduous, I
beg to recommend that C. A. Zung Zoong Oen be granted
an increase in pay as from January, 1940 instead of
January, 1941 when an increase will be due to him.

Mr. Zung was promoted to Clerical Assistant on
January 1, 1938 but without any increase in pay.
Consequently for the past six years he has not received
any increase in wages. His last increase amounted to
$2. only, given on 1.7.33 when his pay as a first
grade clerk reached the maximum.

In view of the fact that in certain cases in
the past persons promoted to C. A. received an increase
either on the date of their promotion or one or two
years afterwards, Mr. Zung's case appears to merit
special consideration particularly as his pay has
remained stationary over so long a period during which
time he has earned many credits as shown by his service
record.

The work of the clerical staff in Section 1,
Special Branch, is unusually heavy and requires an
ability well above the average. Nevertheless the work
has been carried out satisfactorily and efficiently
under the supervision of C.A. Zung who is both assiduous
and painstaking. I therefore respectfully request that
the recommendation be granted.

R.W. Mac Adie
D. S. I.

制作及转呈人：副总督察长 MacAdie

鉴于其持续良好的工作表现以及对既重要又艰巨的职责的奉献精神，我谨建议自1940年1月起（而非原定的1941年1月）给予文案助理程仲安加薪。

程先生于1938年1月1日晋升为文案助理，但未伴随任何加薪。因此，在过去六年中，他未获得任何工资增长。他上一次加薪仅为2元，发生于1933年7月1日，当时他作为一级书记员的薪水已达到最高限额。

鉴于过去在某些情况下，晋升为文案助理的人员要么在晋升之日，要么在一两年后获得了加薪，程先生的情况似乎值得特别考虑，特别是因为他的薪水在如此长的时期内一直停滞不前，而在此期间，正如他的服务记录所示，他赢得了许多嘉奖。

特别支部第一科文案人员的工作量异常繁重，需要远高于平均水平的能力。尽管如此，在勤勉且细致的文案助理程的监督下，工作得以令人满意且高效地完成。因此，我恭敬地请求批准此项建议。

R.W. Mac Adie
副总督察长（D. S. I.）

Sir,
It will be seen from attached reports that
certain discrimination in treatment has been shown
Chinese clerks in Crime and Traffic Branches to the
detriment of clerks attached to Special Branch.
The work of clerks of the Special Branch demands
that they be efficient in every respect and on this
ground alone it is but fair that they receive treat-
ment at least on a par with other Branches. There
is no doubt that there exists in the minds of clerks
and detectives attached to Special Branch the idea
that of
that their treatment is below the staff of Crime
Branch, particularly Headquarters, and I am afraid,
they have grounds for these ideas.
Comparison between advancement of Crime
Branch and Special Branch detectives is a matter
I propose bringing up two months hence before next
year's estimates are called for.
For the time being I strongly recommend
the promotion to 2nd grade of clerks Hsu Ta Yung and
Tan Hsueh-hua and to 1st grade of clerk Wong Chia-tsing.
These employees are exceptionally keen and highly
efficient.
I also recommend the addition of two third
class clerks to cope with the work which has increased
by leaps and bounds during the past six months and
shows no sign of falling off.

警务总监阁下：

从附呈的报告可以看出，刑事科和交通科的华籍文员在待遇上受到某些区别对待，这对特别科的文员不利。特别科文员的工作要求他们在各方面都具备高效率，仅凭这一点，他们理应获得至少与其他各科同等的待遇。毫无疑问，特别科的文员和侦探心中存在一种看法，认为他们的待遇低于刑事科（特别是总部）的职员，而且恐怕这种看法是有根据的。

Subject Chinese Clerical Staff of S.I.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The Chinese clerks in S.I. have voiced a grievance in regard to the recent promotion of clerks in other Sections who joined on or about the same dates and have almost the same length of service as themselves as 3rd grade clerks. Those clerks were promoted to 2nd grade with the consequential increase in salary. One case in point is that of a 3rd grade clerk in the Traffic Branch who joined the Police Force on 6/2/36 and with only three years service was elevated to 2nd grade clerk, the others who are attached to the Finger Print Bureau are from 7 months to a year senior to our senior 3rd grade clerks. It is a fact that the work carried out by the clerks in Special Branch is of a very important nature and that it is carried out efficiently is evidenced by the fact that they have been commended on a number of occasions, therefore all things being equal they should be given consideration when promotions to another grade are being made.

Clerks Hsu Ta Yung and Tan Hsueh Hua both qualify in this respect having joined on the 1/2/35 and 18/3/35 respectively and whose work I can highly recommend both being hard working and energetic and fully deserving of promotion to 2nd grade clerks.

2nd grade clerk Wong Chia Tsing is another who is deserving of recognition. 2nd grade clerks who have less service and who are attached to the Finger Print Bureau were recently elevated to 1st grade.

华籍特别科情报组的文员对近期其他部门文员的晋升表示不满，那些文员加入警队的时间与他们大致相同，服务年限也几乎一样，原本同为三级文员。那些文员已晋升为二级文员，薪资也随之增加。一个典型的例子是交通科的一名三级文员，他于1936年2月6日加入警队，仅服务三年便升为二级文员；而其他隶属于指纹局的文员，其资历比我们资深的三级文员还要多七个月至一年。事实上，特别科文员所从事的工作性质非常重要，其工作效率之高可从他们多次受到嘉奖这一事实得到证明，因此，在同等条件下，在进行级别晋升时应给予他们考虑。

Attached to this report is a chart of suggested
improvement and distribution of staff which will
affect the Chinese members employed in S.I.
It is the considered opinion of the undersigned
that more efficiency will be introduced in the
re-distribution as the bulk of the work has been
falling on two Sub-Inspectors who are both good
men and willing workers but have not the time to
carry out effective supervision. This is
profoundly clear when the number of associations,
guilds, societies, schools, etc., which have been
registered, are taken into consideration.
Applications from these different organisations
for functions of different sorts are continually
arriving and when permitted, which is often, have
to be watched in order to have the police instructions
rigidly enforced. This I think can be considered
as a permanent procedure and therefore will need
persons whole time and means a re-distribution of
the strength and suggest an increase as proposed
in the attached chart.
The food situation in these abnormal times
requires constant watching and needs a person who
is respected and trusted by the people interested
including the Chamber of Commerce and this can be
safely left in the hands of C.D.S. 94 Chang Ying-mei
who has proven his worth in this direction and who
it is recommended be made a Sub-Inspector.

由克劳福德（Crawford）探长撰写并转呈

本报告附件是一份关于改进及人员分配的建议图表，这将影响受雇于华籍特别科情报组的华籍成员。具名者经过深思熟虑认为，重新分配工作将提高效率，因为大部分工作一直压在两名副督察身上，他们虽然都是能干且愿意工作的人，但没有时间进行有效的监督。考虑到已注册的协会、公会、社团、学校等组织的数量，这一点显得尤为清楚。

这些不同组织举办各类活动的申请源源不断，而在获准后（这种情况经常发生），必须进行监视，以确保警务指令得到严格执行。我认为这可以视为一项常规程序，因此需要专人全职负责，这意味着需要重新分配警力，并建议按附件图表所示增加人手。

在这个非常时期，粮食状况需要持续监控，需要一个受到相关人士（包括商会）尊重和信任的人来负责，这项工作可以放心地交给华籍高级侦探94号张英梅（Chang Ying-mei），他在此方面已证明了自己的价值，建议将其提拔为副督察。

Subject Report on work of C.D.C. 357 Liu Te Sien (劉德銑)
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

C.D.C. 357 was transferred to Special Branch for detective duty on January 1, 1937. Since his transfer, his work has not been at all satisfactory. He has been given enquiries and other work which would with an ambitious and diligent detective have produced some results but he appears to have no interest in his work. Only seven months ago, he was brought before the undersigned for general slackness and severely warned. He was also told that his work would in the succeeding months be carefully checked but apparently the warning had no effect as another instance of his slackness came to the notice of his supervising officer D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken. He was detailed for observation duty on Robison Road near the Social Centre on June 15, 1938 in connection with the distribution of the booklet "Unity" which was being carried out through this centre, but between 2 p.m. and 2.30 p.m. he could not be found in that vicinity.
His excuse for leaving his post was that he had some business of his own to attend to and did not return until 2.45 p.m.

C. Crawford
D. I.

CDC. 357 warned that if his work does not improve during next three months D.C. (Special Branch) he will be returned to uniform.

华籍侦探主任357号于1937年1月1日调至特别科担任侦探职务。自调动以来，他的工作表现一直不能令人满意。曾指派他进行调查及其他工作，若换作一名有上进心且勤奋的侦探，本应取得一些成果，但他似乎对工作毫无兴趣。就在七个月前，他因总体工作懈怠被带到具名者面前，并受到严厉警告。当时还告知他，随后几个月将仔细检查他的工作，但显然警告未起作用，因为他的上司副华籍总督察高延根（Kao Yen Ken，音译）又发现了他另一次懈怠的情况。1938年6月15日，他被派往罗宾森路（Robison Road，即今南京西路）社会中心附近执行观察任务，这与通过该中心分发《团结》小册子有关，但在下午2点至2点30分之间，在该区域找不到他。

As matters stand at present I have no hesitation in report-
ing that the clerical staff of S.I. is overworked and as an
instance of this I have to quote the case of D.S.I.Montgomery
who among other matters, has an inquiry the " Social Bureau and
Interference with Savings Departments of Local Stores" and who
has been compelled, owing to lack of Chinese staff, to delay the
progress of investigation. And the same handicap is experienced
by all foreigners attached to S.I. in conducting investigations.
In addition to this, each member of the staff of S.I. has to
take his turn on night duty or duty after office hours.

This system of working at high tension is a great mental
strain on the staff and prevents them from perusing in a studious
manner literature or other documents which might assist them in
the concentration of their efforts in furtherance of their know-
ledge of political and labour matters in order to promote effic-
iency.

The addition of a proposed new 3rd Class Clerk will
not create an increase of staff but will merely bring it up to
normal strength and thereby assist to make up the work that has
fallen behind. The addition of two 3rd Class Clerks, however,
will relieve matters somewhat.

Another serious handicap to the efficient working of
the office is the lack of equipment. At present there are 3
typewriters in S.I. and no provision made in the estimates for
more. This means that three members of the clerical staff of
S.I. each have a type-writer which is almost constantly in use
and in the event of another man being transferred he is immediately
handicapped by the lack of a machine and consequently obliged
to wait until someone else has finished typing before he can

Special Branch Organisation Circular No. 1

The principal duty of Special Branch No. 1 is
to obtain, as far as possible, information of impending
trouble among Chinese in the Settlement or adjoining
districts, and, in the event of actual trouble, to keep
in close touch with members of the public and collect
timely information of events likely to affect law and
order.

The duties of S.1 will include watching and
reporting on all political, quasi-political and popular
religious movements among the Chinese population in
Shanghai. In watching and reporting on the activities
of political associations and labour organizations
formed by Chinese, this section should co-ordinate
these inquiries by daily consultation with the officer
investigating Russian activities. S.1 should be in
a position to supply statistics and information concerning
Military, Naval, Political and Labour matters quickly,
and for this purpose daily compilation and corrections
should be made.

The following classification of the statistics
to be kept and information furnished under the different
headings should enable the Officer i/c of S. 1 and his
subordinates to understand what exactly is expected from them.

Military

Detailed information on the distribution, strength,
armaments, etc. of the Chinese military forces in the
Shanghai district, the progress of war activities in
neighbouring provinces likely to affect local military
situation, particularly in regard to possible effect on the
peace and good order of the Settlement and outlying roads.

特务科组织通告第1号

特务一科的主要职责是尽可能获取租界或邻近地区华人中即将发生的骚乱的情报，并在实际发生骚乱时，与公众保持密切联系，收集可能影响治安的事件的及时信息。

特务一科的职责包括监视和报告上海华人群体中的所有政治、准政治以及民间宗教运动。在监视和报告华人组建的政治团体和劳工组织的活动时，该科应与负责调查俄国活动的警官每日协商，以协调这些调查工作。特务一科应能够迅速提供有关军事、海军、政治和劳工事务的统计数据和信息，为此目的，应每日进行汇编和修正。

以下对需保存的统计数据及按不同类别提供的信息的分类，应能使特务一科主管及其下属确切了解对他们的工作要求。

军事

关于上海地区中国军队的部署、兵力、武器装备等的详细信息，以及邻近省份可能影响当地军事局势的战争活动进展，特别是关于对租界及外围道路和平与良好秩序可能产生的影响。

(C.I.D.) Office Notes

Sir,

Among its multifarious duties, the Intelligence Section keeps a record of Chinese political offenders, the object of which is to have some check on their movements and activities.

No doubt this is one of the most important tasks of this office. Keeping this in view, I respectfully beg to suggest that this service would be greatly facilitated if a photograph of all Chinese arrested by the Municipal Police in connexion with political offences could be obtained by this office.

The importance of having photographs of all such offenders is the more important, because it is a well known fact that such individuals frequently change their names.

Enquiries are very often made as to a certain suspect by the Authorities, but this office is under present conditions only in the most fortunate circumstances in a position to supply the required information.

Without going into every aspect of the question, it must be at once apparent that an up-to-date record containing a copy of photograph together with a description of each individual would be a distinct asset to this Office.

E Papp

A/ D. C. I.
With reference to our conversation this morning,
I shall, subject to your approval, issue the following order:—
"The present practice of forwarding reports
through the Intelligence Section will cease forthwith.
In future the reports from the various sections will be
sent to the C.I.D. Registry which will be held responsible
for attaching relative files and submitting these together
with the original reports direct to the A.D.C.I. Reports made by
subordinate officers of sections must be forwarded through
the officer in charge of the section concerned who should
sign his name in the column "Forwarded by" as evidence
that he had seen it. Officers in charge of Sections
should see that reports are in proper order before they
forward them in this way.
This rule will not apply to the Morning Intelligence
Report and newspaper translations which will be submitted
to the A/D.C.I. as is done at present."

情报股

外籍人员：总督察罗伯逊（Robertson）之职责为：-
对本股进行总体监督。编制《每日情报报告》。调查并报告不时出现之各类杂项事务。就政治案件及劳资纠纷与巡捕房保持联络。通晓一般政治局势及动态。执行由中国当局及临时法院送达之涉及政治犯罪之逮捕令等；对共产主义机关实施突击搜查。

Intelligence Section.

It is the duty of the Intelligence Section to
forward reports about all labour disputes of a serious
nature which come under its notice irrespective of
whether these disputes result in strikes or not.
In cases where dissatisfaction among employees
is removed by negotiation, the facts should be reported
if available.
It should be the ambition of the Intelligence
Section to collect as much useful information as possible
on the labour situation. The extent to which unrest,
which manifests itself in demands for higher wages,
prevails among the workin classes and the means being
employed to remove it come within the category of useful
information.
